title: Did the scheduler attempt to run the job?
summary: Separate scheduler launch failures from commands that launched and failed.

choices.label: Cron launched it but the command failed
It ran but expected business effect is missing

title: Inspect existing scheduler evidence
summary: Use the crontab, scheduler logs, existing mail, and already-configured output redirection. Interactive shell output is not cron execution evidence.

commands.purpose: Inspect the current user crontab without changing it.
Where systemd and these unit names exist, inspect recent scheduler evidence; use the real service/log source for the platform.

choices.label: Existing evidence shows an execution attempt
Existing evidence shows no execution attempt
Existing evidence is insufficient; add temporary bounded instrumentation
Evidence source or ownership is unclear

title: Temporarily capture bounded cron-launched evidence
summary: Add a short-lived diagnostic wrapper or temporary scheduled entry that records only the timestamp, effective user, working directory, selected non-sensitive environment values, exit code, stdout, and stderr from the cron-launched process.

commands.purpose: Illustrative pattern only: write bounded diagnostic output to an owner-restricted temporary file. Replace diagnostic_command with a reviewed wrapper; do not dump the full environment.

choices.label: Temporary evidence captured an execution attempt
Temporary evidence still shows no execution attempt
Safe temporary instrumentation cannot be established

prerequisites: Original crontab or scheduler configuration recorded
Real scheduled user and crontab type confirmed
Controlled temporary output path is permission-restricted
Only selected non-sensitive environment values will be captured
rollback: Remove the temporary diagnostic entry or wrapper, delete the temporary output after review, and restore the exact original crontab/configuration.
verification: No sensitive values remain in diagnostic output
The scheduler and job are rechecked using the original intended configuration.

title: Which scheduler and crontab type are in use?
summary: Service names and file syntax differ across cron implementations and system crontabs.

choices.label: BusyBox, container, macOS, or platform scheduler

title: Is the schedule valid for the actual cron dialect and user timezone?
summary: A command can be correct but never become due.

title: Does the system entry include the required user field and valid file ownership?
summary: System crontabs differ from user crontabs.

choices.label: User field, ownership, or syntax is wrong

title: Inspect the actual scheduler service and logs
summary: Identify cron, crond, BusyBox, or another scheduler before restarting anything.

title: What differs from the successful interactive environment?
summary: Cron commonly has a smaller PATH, different shell, no working-directory assumption, and fewer variables.

title: Did the command exit successfully in the expected user/context?
summary: A launched command can succeed technically but operate on the wrong path, environment, or account.

title: Use platform-specific scheduler evidence
summary: Containers, macOS launchd, and managed schedulers do not follow one Linux cron service model.

title: Continue with shell execution diagnosis
summary: Inspect execute permission, shebang, interpreter, mount options, and real user context; never use chmod 777.

title: Correct the confirmed schedule or system-crontab structure
summary: Change only the validated entry and preserve a copy of the previous schedule.
rollback: Restore the previous crontab entry from the saved copy.
verification: Scheduler attempts execution at the intended time and user.

title: Restore the confirmed scheduler service
summary: Repair the service-specific cause; do not restart blindly without reading failure evidence.
rollback: Restore the previous service configuration and use the last known-good package/unit state.
verification: Scheduler remains running and launches a controlled test job.

title: Make execution context explicit
summary: Use absolute paths, an intentional shell/interpreter, controlled environment sources, and a known working directory.

choices.label: Secret handling or ownership is unclear

rollback: Restore the previous entry/script and remove temporary debug output containing sensitive values.
verification: Job succeeds under the real scheduled user and environment.

title: Control overlapping executions deliberately
summary: Use an appropriate locking or idempotency design after confirming overlap is the cause.
rollback: Remove the new lock wrapper and restore the previous schedule if it blocks legitimate work.
verification: Only intended executions run and missed/overlapping work is handled safely.

title: Verify scheduler, command, and business effect
summary: A log line alone does not prove the intended task completed.
verification: Correct user and environment are used

title: Escalate with crontab type and execution evidence
summary: Record scheduler implementation, user, schedule, timezone, command, and sanitized output without exposing secrets.

title: Diagnosis complete
summary: The reviewed recovery checks passed. Record the cause and prevention step before closing the incident.
prevention: Document the confirmed cause and exact recovery.
Add monitoring or a regression check where practical.
